beside.label: The queued guide change it carries, PGQ-013 (the exercise goes well and ordinary life stays the same)
beside.text:
Suggested reader-facing material to merge with that section without duplicating its existing strategy-review language:

> There is another kind of mismatch to watch for: the inner-child exercise may actually go very well while ordinary life stays almost unchanged. You may find the child, feel real care, say exactly what needed to be said, and still return afterward to the same self-abandonment, hiding, chaos, or choices.
>
> That does not necessarily mean the meditation failed, and it does not necessarily mean you need a deeper or more powerful meditation. It may mean the missing step is transfer.
>
> Ask what the adult actually did in the exercise. Did they nurture, protect, guide, stay present, tell the truth, allow imperfection, or slow something down? Then choose one very small way—five percent is enough—to let that same function appear in ordinary life.
>
> The Nurturer might ask for support or let a safe person see something imperfect. The Protector might rest, set a boundary, leave an overwhelming situation, or stop using another person as a test. The Guide might choose one realistic next step instead of demanding certainty first.
>
> The child does not have to believe the new adult immediately. Words become more credible when ordinary life begins to match them. One small act of follow-through can sometimes teach more than repeating an already-successful meditation ten more times.
>
> Then review what happened without turning the review into another judgment of your worth. The question is simply whether this action made the caring, protective, or guiding function a little more real outside the exercise, and what should be kept or adjusted next time.

Preserve these limits: do not require homework after every meditation; do not treat one outward act as generalized adult capacity; do not call weak carryover proof that the meditation was fake or that reparenting failed.

## Pending bundle D — blocked action, conversational continuity, and memory support

Upstream authority: `AMEND.CROSS.BLOCKED_ACTION_WAIT`, `AMEND.CROSS.SUPPORT_MODE_CONTINUITY`, `AMEND.CROSS.MEMORY_VS_REFLECTIVE_JOURNALING`, `AMEND.CROSS.PRACTICAL_FOCUS_SEQUENCING`, and the corresponding runtime/graph rules.

beside.label: The queued guide change it carries, PGQ-016 (memory support is not the same as reflective journaling)
beside.text: Preserve the distinction between meaning-making journals and low-interpretation external memory. When reflective journaling makes experience more confusing, a short dated fact log, what-helped note, reminder, next-step entry, or voice note can preserve continuity without requiring simultaneous interpretation. Pattern-finding can happen later if useful; a memory aid does not need to explain the person's life.
